transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Lina Torres, Markus Hale, Rosa Jimenez (BlueZephyr)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/bench/bluezephyr-2026-11, https://docs.redwood.ai/security/attestations, bench-sheets/quant-tune-v2.xlsx

[00:00] Ethan Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is this still good for 45ish minutes?
[00:04] Lina Torres: Yep, perfect. We have about an hour blocked but 45 works.
[00:10] Ethan Morales: Great. Quick agenda — recap last week's runs, go over the fresh bench numbers we pushed to the sheet, then Priya will walk through the routing/kv-cache tweak we applied on the dedicated slots, and we'll triage tail latency. Any additions?
[00:20] Markus Hale: Maybe a quick security micro ask — Rosa has a question about KMS rotation and audit logs, but we can do that at the end if time.
[00:25] Rosa Jimenez: Yes, just a brief confirmation, we need to confirm HSM integration options and retention windows.
[00:30] Ethan Morales: Perfect, we'll leave 10 minutes at the end. Ok, Priya over to you for the numbers.

[02:05] Priya Kapoor: Thanks. So we re-ran the baseline vs Redwood tunings over the weekend with your sample traffic (thanks Markus). I updated the sheet at the link, key highlights: p50 is basically flat against your incumbent, p95 improved from 340ms to 220ms on our tuned quant+kv cache, p99 though is still at around 820ms — so tail is the work item. Those numbers are for the 512-token prompt set, mixed user patterns.
[02:36] Lina Torres: Wait, those p95 numbers look good. How did you get that delta — was it primarily quantization or the routing fallback?
[02:45] Priya Kapoor: It's a mix. Quantization (we used 4-bit hybrid on the attention kernels) shaved about 12% on token compute. The bigger win came from prefix KV caching — since your load has high prefix reuse ~35% we saw much fewer KV cache misses. Also we adjusted the batch window policy to be a shorter window at peak to keep latency SLO.

[03:30] Markus Hale: Quick question, when you say 4-bit hybrid, are we losing top-level accuracy? We can't drop below our 97.2% NER F1 threshold.
[03:42] Priya Kapoor: We validated accuracy on your eval set — delta was negligible, like 0.2 absolute on F1 in synthetic runs. I'm honest there's a small wobble on a tiny subset of outliers — we flagged those in the sheet. If you want, we can run the same with 8-bit per-layer selectively for those heads.

[04:15] Lina Torres: Good. For throughput, how did Redwood perform under our burst test? We ran 200 concurrent streams for 3 minutes.
[04:25] Priya Kapoor: Under that burst, the raw throughput (tokens/s) was about 18% higher than the incumbent when using dedicated slots. However we saw a higher error/retry rate during burst spikes — roughly 1.8% vs incumbent 1.1% — that's tied to our autoscaler bump timing and some transient OOMs when KV cache populated, which we patched in the afternoon run.
[05:01] Ethan Morales: To reiterate, the retry spike is operational, not model regressions. We pushed an autoscaler config to extend the warm-up to 60s which dropped retries to 0.4% in the validation run. The Saturday run is the one with the OOMs.

[05:40] Rosa Jimenez: For security, can someone clarify where the cached prefixes live — are they in encrypted RAM in the tenant boundary? We can't have unencrypted KV in disk.
[05:54] Priya Kapoor: Good call. The KV cache lives in-GPU memory or instance RAM, never persisted to disk in the default config. For Private deployments you can tie the cache memory to host-level encryption; for Dedicated we offer a tenant-resident encrypted RAM option. We'll share the KMS/HSM integration doc.

[06:30] Lina Torres: The p99 tail — any immediate hypothesis?
[06:36] Priya Kapoor: Two main suspects: 1) request coalescing edge cases where huge requests stall smaller tokens while batch waits (we tuned window but edge still exists), 2) rare long-run KV eviction thrash when your traffic spikes with diverse prefixes. We can instrument per-request traces to isolate.

[07:10] Markus Hale: Can we get those traces with anonymized content? We can share a scrubbed set.
[07:16] Ethan Morales: Absolutely — we can work with your infra to accept scrubbed traces. We'll provide a tracer that strips PII.

[07:40] Priya Kapoor: Also we ran a routing variant — fallback to a slightly cheaper-sized variant during off-peak; that cut costs ~9% and had negligible impact to p95, but p99 moved only marginally. So routing helps economics more than tail.

[08:05] Lina Torres: Hmm, incumbent seems more stable on the tail; is that because they keep a larger warm pool?
[08:12] Priya Kapoor: Yep, incumbent keeps a warmer pool which reduces tail; it's a higher steady cost. Our approach is to reduce steady spending via smarter batching and cache, then provide optional reservable slots if you need consistent tail SLOs.

[09:00] Markus Hale: Let's talk about the latency deltas by route. We have 3 routes production uses: short prompts (64 tokens), mid (256), long (512). Were these separated in the sheet?
[09:12] Priya Kapoor: Yes split by route. Short prompts: p95 90ms -> 78ms (small win), mid: 220ms -> 160ms, long: 420ms -> 300ms. Long route is where tail matters.

[09:45] Lina Torres: Could we map which routes saw more KV reuse?
[09:50] Priya Kapoor: Mid had highest reuse, short second, long had the least reuse so it's more compute bound. We recommend a small promt pre-processing cache for long prompts to increase reuse — will add to the playbook.

[10:20] Ethan Morales: Quick pause — any blockers to running a focused rerun this week with our new autoscaler and the per-route warm pool set to 2x for long-route?
[10:32] Markus Hale: We'll schedule the rerun overnight Friday. We'll need the exact config steps and the exact docker image tag.
[10:38] Priya Kapoor: We'll send a runbook and image tag in the follow-up email.

[11:00] Rosa Jimenez: On compliance, is Redwood generating audit logs for each key rotation and who accessed keys? We need proof-of-access logs for SOC reviews.
[11:12] Ethan Morales: Yes, Redwood's Dedicated includes per-request audit logs and KMS access events; we'll provide the SOC2 report and the key rotation artifacts. For Private installs we can map to your HSM and forward logs to your SIEM.

[11:45] Lina Torres: About model quality — we did a quick sample check and saw a small regression on a pattern that affects redaction detection. Is that from quant or from any kernel changes?
[11:56] Priya Kapoor: Likely quant, specifically on the tokenization boundary for certain tokens. We can run a targeted eval with quant disabled on just the final layer and compare. That usually fixes minor redaction regressions.

[12:35] Markus Hale: If we do partial 8-bit on the final layer, what is the inferred cost delta?
[12:42] Priya Kapoor: Rough ballpark 4-6% on unit cost. We'll put the exact numbers in the bench sheet.

[13:05] Ethan Morales: Ok, let's capture explicit next steps — Priya will push a new bench run config with autoscaler warm-up and per-route warm pool set; Ethan will share the quant config and bench link; Markus will run the overnight test and share scrubbed traces for tail analysis; Rosa to confirm compliance checklist items we should provide.

[13:50] Lina Torres: Quick note — our product decides on timeouts at the API gateway level; currently it's 1.2s p99 gate. If Redwood p99 is above that, we will have to adjust gateway settings, so tail matters.
[14:05] Priya Kapoor: Understood. We'll prioritize tail so you don't hit gateway timeouts.

[14:40] Ethan Morales: Any questions about cost modeling or the dedicated slots pricing? We included a comparison row in the sheet showing steady cost with warmer pool vs lean config.
[14:51] Markus Hale: Could you push a scenario where we keep a minimal warm pool for 20% of peak and rely on burst capacity? We want to understand price/perf tradeoffs.
[15:00] Ethan Morales: Yes, will include a 3-scenario table: (1) lean (our default), (2) hybrid warm pool, (3) fully provisioned warm pool like incumbent.

[15:35] Priya Kapoor: One more ops note — we instrumented per-route tracing that correlates KV hit rates to request latencies; adding that to the sheet so you can filter.

[16:00] Rosa Jimenez: Last security question — can audit logs be forwarded to our Splunk with a dedicated forwarder and are they tamper-evident?
[16:10] Ethan Morales: Yes, logs can be forwarded and signed; we provide a checksum bundle and optional attestation signed by an HSM. We'll open a ticket with Security to align on formats.

[16:40] Lina Torres: Sounds good. Anything else?
[16:44] Markus Hale: Naa, we'll run the overnight and send traces.
[16:50] Ethan Morales: Awesome. Recap of next steps: we'll send quant config and bench links, Priya sends runbook + image tag, Markus runs overnight and returns scrubbed traces, Rosa gets SOC/KMS artifacts. We'll meet next Friday same time to review the rerun.

[17:20] Lina Torres: Thanks all.
[17:25] Ethan Morales: Thanks — we'll follow up with artifacts. Bye.

End of transcript.
notes: Bench sheet: per-route breakdown and scenario cost model added by Redwood
Autoscaler warm-up change reduced retry rate in validation run
Tail latency remains primary open issue; customer to provide scrubbed traces
